method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, data cell and call target was compared with those listings by a second pass that re-read the bytes. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and script counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Direct call counts, descriptor names, script argument counts, return counts and constants come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the thirteen CharaBase registrations that set the nameplate color and icon, set the map marker, direct the look-at records, turn the chara back and wait for the turn, set the visible flag and the floating offset, and run the chara scheduler against a target: _setNameplateColor, _setNameplateIcon, _setMapMarker, _lookAtCharacter, _lookAtPosition, _cancelLookAt, _getLookAtCharacter, _turnBack, _waitForTurning, _setVisible, _setFloatingOffset, _getFloatingOffset and _runCharaSchedulerAgainstTarget. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists with the tag checks, the Lua pushes of every branch including an absent receiver, the engine state read and written, the messages sent, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish nameplate content, marker kinds, look-at timing or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers and the world object chain. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller, and each name literal is pushed by one instruction, recorded as nameReference. Each callback address appears once in the image, in its registrar. The switchboard has 81 calls and the orders 28, 32 and 56 are natives of the nameplate and scheduler contracts.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback, so a receiver that is not a CharaBase reaches none of these callbacks. The only wrapper with the non-const holder is the one of _setMapMarker.

framework.identityLookup: 0x004D9970 adds 0x4AC to its receiver and jumps to 0x004DE190. facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x00740020 makes five entries. Registry entry 0 gives the int and entry 1 gives the four floats, the first directly and the others through 0x007282C0, 0x00727290 and 0x00725140. The return list builder 0x0072B440 makes none.

It reaches the world object through 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04 and takes Z, the dword at Y +0x04. It calls 0x0075B570 on Z with the address of the receiver identity from ExecuteParameters +0x0C, the int and the four floats.

0x0075B570 resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 on the first dword of Z and returns when the result is null. Otherwise it forms the address chara +0xBA0 and calls the routine at vtable offset +0x08 of that subobject with the int and the four floats.

The NamePlate vtable 0x00FCF98C holds 0x006A3AD0 at offset +0x08, cell 0x00FCF994. The routine stores the first float at record +0x04, the second at +0x08, the third at +0x0C and the fourth at +0x00 of the record at this +0x68 + n * 0x10. No range test precedes the stores.
For n equal to 1 the routine returns after the stores. For any other n it calls 0x006A3380 with n and then 0x00938020 on the object that 0x006A3380 returns, with a copy of the four floats, 0 and 1.

The four floats are a color. The first three are components and the fourth is an alpha stored first. The role comes from the stored order and from the shipped constants, which lie between 0 and 1 and end in 1 at 19 of 22 sites.

The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071BC90 and cell 1 through 0x0071BAC0, each after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure. 0x0071BC90 casts a non-null control from LuaControl to CharaBase with 0x009DA6CC. A failed cast or a cell with another tag, Nil included, reaches 0x00CCA730 and the reader returns the address of the static zero holder 0x0134B488.

It converts the control to an identity through 0x00CC73B0 on ExecuteParameters +0x04 and stores the identity dword. 0x00CC73B0 passes the control to 0x00CD7A30, which returns 0 for a null control, and passes that result to 0x00CC7030, which loads the dword at +0x70 of it and stores it in the output slot.

It reaches the world object through 0x00CC7510, takes W, the dword at Y, and calls 0x0075C580 on W with the address of the receiver identity from ExecuteParameters +0x0C, the address of the target identity and the float.

0x0075C580 resolves the receiver through 0x004D9970 without a null test and calls 0x00589260 on the chara with the target identity, the float and 0. 0x00589260 calls 0x00587F80 with the slot 0, the priority 0xC8, the identity, the float and the flag 0.

0x00587F80 calls 0x00585F60 twice, once for each bank 0 and 1. 0x00585F60 replaces a target equal to the dword at chara +0x88 with 0xC0000000, skips the bank when the byte at record +0x02 is above the priority, and otherwise writes the record. Flag bit 0 is cleared, bits 1 and 4 are set and bits 2 and 3 are cleared for the flag 0. The priority goes to +0x02, the byte 0 to +0x03, the identity to +0x04, the float to +0x18 and a zero byte to +0x08.

A record sits at chara +0x290 + (slot + 3 * bank) * 0x30. Bank 0 starts at +0x290 and bank 1 at +0x320. The chara initialization constructs an array of 6 elements of 0x30 bytes at +0x290 through the array constructor 0x009D61D6 with the element constructor 0x0058F130, which matches 3 slots in 2 banks.

The identity written to +0x04 is the character to face. The float is a rate or duration. The roles come from the native names and from the corpus values 0.25, 0.5 and 1, and no consumer of the records was traced.

The declared list has 3 entries, so the marshaller supplies a tag 6 placeholder for a missing position. For a Nil cell 2 it calls 0x0075C440 with the address of the receiver identity, the scheduler int and the address of the target identity.

For another cell 2 it reads an int through 0x005819A0, zero extends its low word and calls 0x0075C470 with the address of the receiver identity, the scheduler int, the address of the target identity and the word.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.

The identity lookup returns 0 for an identity that is not in the registry. Every glue routine except the nameplate pair uses the result without a null test, so the run-time effect of an absent receiver was not run for any of them.

The nameplate part and icon category numbers have no range test. The size of the NamePlate record array, the child control array and the icon cache, and the bodies of 0x006A3380, 0x00938020 and 0x0096A010, were not traced.

The consumers of the look-at records at chara +0x290 and +0x320, the roles of the flag bits and of the float at record +0x18 were not traced. _getLookAtCharacter reads other storage and does not read these records.
The consumers of the scene messages 0x3B, 0x48, 0x10 and 0x11, the class of the object at chara +0x84 and the producer of the event type 0x4A were not traced.
The consumers of chara +0x270, +0x3E4, +0x438 and of the pending marker object at NpcBase +0x128, and the code that applies a pending object, were not traced.
The writers of the dword at chara +0x12C and of NpcBase +0x154, and the meaning of the work value at the key 0x0BBE with the element offset 2, were not traced.
A null target control reaches 0x00CC7030 with a null object after 0x00CD7A30 returns 0. The run-time effect and the behavior of the error report 0x00CCA730 for a Nil control cell were not run.
The yield request 0x00CD2860 of _waitForTurning was recorded as a call. Whether it polls the checker once before it suspends was not traced.

The classes derived from CharaBase are INFERRED from a comparison of the first 60 cells of every Lua control vftable with the CharaBase vftable. Only the PlayerBase, MyPlayer and NpcBase vftables share more than 26 cells. A derived class with an unusual vftable would not be found by that comparison.

Whether the marshaller 0x00D19A20 can yield a cell vector of a size other than the declared count for _runCharaSchedulerAgainstTarget was not traced. Such a vector takes the int read path through 0x0075C470 even when cell 2 is Nil.
